topic.label: Classical Physics
topic.desc: Classical physics: Newtonian mechanics, conservation laws, oscillations and waves, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, optics, fluids and relativity.

concepts: Motion, forces, rotation and orbits under Newton's laws.
Work, energy, momentum and the conservation laws used to solve problems.
Oscillators, damping, resonance, wave propagation and interference.
Heat, entropy, thermodynamic cycles and the kinetic theory of gases.
Electric and magnetic fields, circuits and Maxwell's equations.
Geometric and wave optics: lenses, mirrors, diffraction and polarization.
Fluid statics and flow: pressure, viscosity, turbulence and scaling.
Spacetime, time dilation and gravity as curvature, treated as classical field theory.
skills: Solves motion problems with forces, constraints and friction and checks the answer against limiting cases.
Computes torque, moment of inertia and angular momentum for rotating bodies and tops.
Computes orbits, transfer maneuvers and periods under gravity with Kepler's laws and numerical integration, for example orbits around the Moon or a planet and the surface gravity there.
Applies work-energy and potential energy methods and accounts for dissipated energy explicitly.
Solves elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions from momentum and energy balance.
Solves driven and damped oscillators and finds resonance frequency and quality factor.
Analyzes superposition, standing waves, dispersion and interference with Fourier decomposition.
Analyzes engines and refrigerators on pressure-volume diagrams and computes efficiency against the Carnot limit.
Solves conduction, convection and radiation problems with boundary conditions and reports the dominant mode.
Derives gas properties from molecular statistics and connects entropy to counting of states.
Computes fields and potentials of charge distributions with Gauss's law, symmetry and image methods.
Analyzes resistor, capacitor and inductor circuits in steady state and in transients.
Applies Maxwell's equations to waves, radiation and induction and checks boundary conditions.
Traces rays through lenses and mirrors and designs simple optical systems with aberration estimates.
Analyzes diffraction, interference and polarization patterns from slits, gratings and thin films.
Solves pressure, Bernoulli and pipe-flow problems and identifies laminar or turbulent regimes.
Builds dimensionless numbers such as the Reynolds number and uses them to scale models to full size.
Computes time dilation, length contraction and relativistic energy and momentum with Lorentz transformations.

Explains gravity as spacetime curvature, geodesics and gravitational time dilation and separates the weak-field limit from the full theory Compares weight and surface gravity on the Moon, Mars and Earth.
